subject: fix-cli-standalone
kind: deliver
result: pass
revision: 5530668c970b18fc76a90f447874d1b9d67c5fbf
evidence: Reproduced the original failure by pip-installing the checkout into `/tmp/opencode/cli-repro` and running with empty HOME: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'affidavit'` at `orchestra/cli.py:11 -> close_batch.py:49`. After the fix, reinstalled to `/tmp/opencode/cli-repro2` and ran `orchestra --help` and `orchestra contract --path` with empty HOME/no affidavit on PATH/PYTHONPATH: exit 0, contract path resolves inside the installed prefix. Test runs from the worktree: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_cli_packaging.py -q -k standalone` -> 1 passed, 3 deselected; full `tests/test_cli_packaging.py` -> 4 passed; `tests/test_cli_packaging.py tests/test_affidavit_import_boundary.py tests/test_close_batch.py tests/test_orchestra_commands.py` -> 65 passed; `tests/test_affidavit_check.py tests/test_verify_authority.py tests/test_evidence_loop.py tests/test_record_bind_policy.py tests/test_orchestra_commands.py` -> 52 passed. Working tree clean after commit.
observations: `check` and `install` were exercised via `--help`; `install --dry-run` in the standalone environment correctly reports the missing installer package (exit 2, no traceback). `close-batch` still passes all oracle-adapter tests when affidavit is available.
root_cause: `orchestra.cli` imported `orchestra.close_batch` at module scope, and `close_batch` imported `affidavit.oracle_red` at module scope, so every console-script invocation required a `~/affidavit` checkout (or `AFFIDAVIT_ROOT`/`aff` on PATH).
verdict: pass
metrics: 1 standalone test; 4 packaging tests; 65 related tests; 52 regression tests.
claim: An installed `orchestra` console script now serves `check`, `install`, `contract`, `project-field`, and `sessions` with an empty HOME and no affidavit checkout on PATH/PYTHONPATH, while `close-batch` keeps its oracle adapter when present and explains its absence otherwise.
